summary: 30 ft steel lookout on Grizzly Mountain, Ferry County, WA; built 1941 on the Colville Indian Reservation, abandoned 1952, still standing and holding antennas.

facts.design: 30-foot steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab

access.note: On the Colville Indian Reservation. No page read states a visitor rule; the permission level is the record's classification. Check with the land managers before going.

visit.trail_note: Road reaches near the summit with high-clearance 4WD for the last mile (WillhiteWeb, visit date not stated); a 2019 visit stopped about two miles short after a downed tree. Do not climb: missing boards and side rails.

events.note: 30-foot steel tower with 7x7 ft cab; no source gives the reason for building it
Ground cabin and roof were lost in the years after abandonment
Summit Trail fire, started by lightning on July 12, threatened the lookout per TrailChick; the sources read do not say what happened to the tower

corrections.why: All three sources describe a 30-foot (about 9.1 m) steel tower. The 2.1 m figure matches none of them.

corrections.proposed: Remove from Grizzly's history. The 1938 removal was of an identical tower at Moses Mountain, which this tower may have come from.
corrections.why: The sources tie the 1938 removal to Moses Mountain, not to Grizzly, and they describe the Moses link as a possibility only.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WillhiteWeb (visit date not stated) describes a road that reaches the lookout with high-clearance 4WD needed for the last mile. TrailChick (visited 2019) stopped about two miles short after a downed tree. These describe different visits and possibly different road conditions, so both are kept and the story gives TrailChick's year.

notes_for_editor: Read: firelookout.com, TrailChick, WillhiteWeb and the firelookout.org list (plus a weebly index page that only lists Colville Indian Reservation). Not read: the Moses Mountain page, SummitPost, HistoryLink. The brief's height_m (2.1) and 1938 removal event are corrected. The Moses Mountain origin is a claim all three sites repeat as 'may have come from', so it is kept hedged. No staffing, fire-watch or rental information was found. The access level 'permission' comes from the record and is not stated by any source read; the reservation-land location is sourced. Whether the 2021 Summit Trail fire damaged the tower is unknown. The road description mixes an undated WillhiteWeb visit (its page mentions 2016 washouts) and a 2019 TrailChick visit.
